units.previous_finding: Two eligible teaching comments retain clear generic-English language defects. “pages starting with url, to a maximum of depth.” is grammatically awkward, and “fakeFetcher is Fetcher that returns canned results.” is missing the ordinary article before the type-description noun phrase. These are translatable natural-language comments rather than protected Go/code identity. The issues do not change technical meaning, but they prevent the candidate from meeting the A-level requirement for natural, polished English (Singapore) and require a minor revision.
